title: Technical Research & RFC Synthesis — GraphRAG Integration
buyerQuestion: Can Oddjob automate end-to-end technical research into a published RFC and engineering backlog, with human governance at critical decision points?

researchTopic.title: Integrating GraphRAG into Oddjob's Qdrant-based RAG Pipeline
researchTopic.description: GraphRAG extends traditional vector-similarity retrieval by layering a knowledge graph over chunked embeddings, enabling multi-hop reasoning and relationship-aware context assembly. This research investigates how GraphRAG techniques can augment Oddjob's existing Qdrant-backed retrieval pipeline to improve answer grounding, reduce hallucination, and surface cross-document relationships that flat semantic search misses.
researchTopic.rationale: This topic is ideal for the golden demo because it is self-referential — Oddjob researching how to improve its own RAG pipeline — which exercises every mission naturally: literature discovery surfaces real papers, technology triage forces an architecture decision between hybrid approaches, feasibility audits inspect existing Qdrant service code, PoC sign-off evaluates a working prototype, RFC synthesis compiles findings into an actionable document, and backlog hydration decomposes implementation into trackable engineering tasks.

knowledge.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
knowledge.content: This paper introduces GraphRAG, a method that extends retrieval-augmented generation by constructing a knowledge graph over the source corpus using LLM-generated entity and relationship extractions. The key innovation is a two-stage pipeline: first, community detection algorithms (Leiden) partition the graph into hierarchical clusters, then each community is pre-summarized into natural-language descriptions. At query time, the system performs either local retrieval (entity-neighborhood traversal for specific questions) or global retrieval (community-summary map-reduce for broad sensemaking queries), significantly outperforming naive vector-similarity RAG on comprehensiveness and diversity metrics.

knowledge.title: Oddjob RAG Architecture: Qdrant Vector Retrieval Pipeline
knowledge.content: Oddjob's current RAG pipeline ingests documents by chunking them into overlapping segments (512 tokens, 64-token overlap), generating embeddings via the configured AI provider, and upserting vectors into a Qdrant collection partitioned by organization. At query time, the rag-service performs top-K similarity search (k=5 default) against the organization's collection, retrieves matching chunks with metadata, and injects them as context into the LLM system prompt. The pipeline supports filtering by knowledge topic and document recency but lacks any relationship-aware traversal or multi-hop reasoning capability.

knowledge.title: RAG Service Integration Points — Current Implementation
knowledge.content: The RAG subsystem is implemented across three key files: `server/services/rag-service.ts` handles embedding generation, Qdrant upsert/query, and context assembly; `server/services/knowledge-service.ts` manages CRUD operations for knowledge documents and topics; and the shared schema defines `knowledgeNodes` and `knowledgeEdges` tables in `shared/schema/knowledge.ts` which already store entity-relationship data extracted during pipeline executions. The knowledge-service exposes graph traversal methods (`getConnectedNodes`, `getEdgesByType`) that are currently used only for UI visualization but could serve as the foundation for graph-enhanced retrieval.

knowledge.title: Hybrid Retrieval Pattern: Vector Similarity + Graph Traversal
knowledge.content: The hybrid retrieval pattern combines dense vector search with structured graph traversal to produce context that captures both semantic similarity and relational proximity. The approach works in three stages: first, vector similarity search identifies seed entities from the query embedding; second, graph traversal follows typed relationships outward from seed nodes for N hops (typically 2–3), collecting connected entities and their attributes; third, results from both paths are merged using reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) which normalizes rankings across heterogeneous retrieval signals. This pattern requires maintaining a synchronized knowledge graph alongside the vector index but delivers measurably better recall on multi-hop questions.

artifacts.title: Hybrid Retrieval Service — GraphRAG Integration PoC
RFC-2024-007: GraphRAG Integration into Oddjob Knowledge Pipeline
artifacts.content:
# RFC-2024-007: GraphRAG Integration

## Problem Statement
Oddjob's current RAG pipeline relies solely on vector similarity search, which cannot follow entity relationships or answer multi-hop questions spanning multiple documents.

## Proposed Solution
Integrate a hybrid retrieval layer that combines Qdrant vector search with graph traversal over the existing knowledgeNodes/knowledgeEdges tables. The system will:
1. Extract entities during document indexing
2. Perform parallel vector + graph retrieval at query time
3. Merge results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion
4. Optionally generate community summaries for global queries

## Alternatives Considered
- Option A (Pure Vector): No graph traversal — insufficient for multi-hop queries
- Option B (Full Graph DB): Neo4j-backed — too much infrastructure overhead
- Option C (Hybrid — SELECTED): Reuse existing Postgres graph + Qdrant vectors

## Migration Plan
1. Add graphRagEnabled flag to knowledge_topics table
2. Implement entity extraction during document indexing
3. Build HybridRetrievalEngine service
4. Integrate with existing rag-service.ts as opt-in mode
5. Add community detection background job (async)

## Risks
- Graph traversal adds ~200ms latency (mitigated by caching hot paths)
- Entity extraction quality depends on LLM accuracy (mitigated by confidence thresholds)

documents.title: RFC-2024-007: GraphRAG Integration into Oddjob Knowledge Pipeline

tasks.summary: Add graphRagEnabled flag to knowledge_topics schema
tasks.description: Add a boolean column `graphRagEnabled` (default: false) to the knowledge_topics table. This flag controls whether a topic uses hybrid GraphRAG retrieval or falls back to standard vector-only search. Includes schema migration and shared type updates.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] New `graphRagEnabled` boolean column added to knowledge_topics table
- [ ] Default value is `false` for backward compatibility
- [ ] Drizzle migration generated and tested
- [ ] Shared TypeScript types updated to reflect new column
- [ ] Existing topics unaffected (all default to false)

tasks.summary: Implement HybridRetrievalEngine service with graph traversal
tasks.description: Build the core HybridRetrievalEngine that performs parallel vector similarity search (via Qdrant) and graph traversal (via knowledgeEdges table), then merges results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion. The service is invoked when a topic has graphRagEnabled=true.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] HybridRetrievalEngine class created in server/services/
- [ ] Vector search stage queries Qdrant for top-K seed entities
- [ ] Graph traversal stage follows knowledgeEdges up to configurable maxHops
- [ ] RRF merge combines both result sets with normalized scoring
- [ ] Latency < 500ms for 2-hop traversal on typical topic graphs
- [ ] Unit tests cover each retrieval stage independently
- [ ] Integration test validates end-to-end hybrid retrieval

tasks.summary: Add community detection background job for GraphRAG topics
tasks.description: Implement an asynchronous background job that runs community detection (Label Propagation algorithm) over the knowledge graph for topics with graphRagEnabled=true. Communities are pre-summarized using LLM and stored for global query retrieval.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] Background job registered in the job scheduler
- [ ] Label Propagation algorithm groups knowledge nodes into communities
- [ ] Each community receives an LLM-generated natural language summary
- [ ] Summaries stored in knowledge_communities table (new migration)
- [ ] Job runs asynchronously after document indexing completes
- [ ] Job is idempotent and can be safely re-run

tasks.description: Wire the HybridRetrievalEngine into the existing rag-service.ts as an opt-in retrieval mode. When a knowledge topic has graphRagEnabled=true, the rag-service delegates to HybridRetrievalEngine instead of performing direct Qdrant vector search.
tasks.acceptanceCriteria:
- [ ] rag-service.ts checks graphRagEnabled flag before retrieval
- [ ] If enabled, delegates to HybridRetrievalEngine
- [ ] If disabled, falls back to existing vector-only path (no behavior change)
- [ ] Response format remains compatible with existing consumers
- [ ] Feature flag can be toggled per-topic without restart
- [ ] Integration test validates both code paths
